title: Al-Hidaya
author: al-marghinani
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Al-Marghinani's concise Hanafi manual with its own commentary, covering worship, transactions, family law, inheritance, procedure and penalties. Its brevity and precision made it the standard statement of Hanafi law in South and Central Asia and the basis of Charles Hamilton's colonial-era Hedaya.
historicalContext: Written in Marghinan in present-day Uzbekistan at the end of the twelfth century, the work distilled the Hanafi tradition into a text a student could memorise and a judge could consult. Its commentary explains the reasoning behind each ruling and records the disagreements of Abu Hanifa's students.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
